segs.e: Linked Discourses 7.1
1. The Perfected Ones
With Dhanañjānī
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the squirrels’ feeding ground.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena aññatarassa bhāradvājagottassa brāhmaṇassa dhanañjānī nāma brāhmaṇī abhippasannā hoti buddhe ca dhamme ca saṅghe ca.
segs.e: Now at that time the wife of a certain brahmin of the Bhāradvāja clan, a brahmin lady named Dhanañjānī, was devoted to the Buddha, the teaching, and the Saṅgha.

segs.p: Atha kho dhanañjānī brāhmaṇī bhāradvājagottassa brāhmaṇassa bhattaṁ upasaṁharantī upakkhalitvā tikkhattuṁ udānaṁ udānesi:
segs.e: Once, while she was bringing her husband his meal, she tripped and expressed this heartfelt sentiment three times:
“Homage to him, the blessed one, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha!
Homage to him, the blessed one, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha!
Homage to him, the blessed one, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha!”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, bhāradvājagotto brāhmaṇo dhanañjāniṁ brāhmaṇiṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When she said this, the brahmin said to Dhanañjānī:

segs.p: “evamevaṁ panāyaṁ vasalī yasmiṁ vā tasmiṁ vā tassa muṇḍakassa samaṇassa vaṇṇaṁ bhāsati.
segs.e: “That’d be right. For the slightest thing this lowlife woman praises that shaven ascetic.

segs.p: Idāni tyāhaṁ, vasali, tassa satthuno vādaṁ āropessāmī”ti.
segs.e: Right now, lowlife woman, I’m going to refute your teacher’s doctrine!”

segs.p: “Na khvāhaṁ taṁ, brāhmaṇa, passāmi sadevake loke samārake sabrahmake sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiyā pajāya sadevamanussāya, yo tassa bhagavato vādaṁ āropeyya arahato sammāsambuddhassa.
segs.e: “Brahmin, I don’t see anyone in this world—with its gods, Māras, and divinities, this population with its ascetics and brahmins, its gods and humans—who can refute the doctrine of the Blessed One, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha.

segs.p: Api ca tvaṁ, brāhmaṇa, gaccha, gantvā vijānissasī”ti.
segs.e: But anyway, you should go. When you’ve gone you’ll understand.”

segs.p: Atha kho bhāradvājagotto brāhmaṇo kupito anattamano yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṁ sammodi.
segs.e: Then the brahmin of the Bhāradvāja clan, angry and upset, went to the Buddha and exchanged greetings with him.

segs.p: Sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi.
segs.e: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side,

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho bhāradvājagotto brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṁ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi:
segs.e: and addressed the Buddha in verse:
“When what is slain do you sleep at ease?
segs.s: the brahmin of the Bhāradvāja clan

segs.e: When what is slain is there no sorrow?
segs.s: the brahmin of the Bhāradvāja clan

segs.e: What is the one thing
segs.s: the brahmin of the Bhāradvāja clan

segs.e: whose killing you approve?”
segs.s: the brahmin of the Bhāradvāja clan

segs.e: “When anger’s slain you sleep at ease.
When anger’s slain there is no sorrow.
Anger has a poisonous root
and a sweet tip, O brahmin.
The noble ones praise its killing,
for when it’s slain there is no sorrow.”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, bhāradvājagotto brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When he said this, the brahmin said to the Buddha,
“Excellent, worthy Gotama! Excellent!

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bho gotama, nikkujjitaṁ vā ukkujjeyya, paṭicchannaṁ vā vivareyya, mūḷhassa vā maggaṁ ācikkheyya, andhakāre vā telapajjotaṁ dhāreyya: ‘cakkhumanto rūpāni dakkhantī’ti; evamevaṁ bhotā gotamena anekapariyāyena dhammo pakāsito.
segs.e: As if he were righting the overturned, or revealing the hidden, or pointing out the path to the lost, or lighting a lamp in the dark so people with clear eyes can see what’s there, worthy Gotama has made the teaching clear in many ways.

segs.p: Esāhaṁ, bhante, bhagavantaṁ gotamaṁ saraṇaṁ gacchāmi dhammañca bhikkhusaṅghañca.
segs.e: I go for refuge to the worthy Gotama, to the teaching, and to the mendicant Saṅgha.

segs.p: Labheyyāhaṁ bhoto gotamassa santike pabbajjaṁ, labheyyaṁ upasampadan”ti.
segs.e: May I receive the going forth, the ordination in the worthy Gotama’s presence?”

segs.p: Alattha kho bhāradvājagotto brāhmaṇo bhagavato santike pabbajjaṁ, alattha upasampadaṁ.
segs.e: And the brahmin received the going forth, the ordination in the Buddha’s presence.

segs.p: Acirūpasampanno kho panāyasmā bhāradvājo eko vūpakaṭṭho appamatto ātāpī pahitatto viharanto nacirasseva—yassatthāya kulaputtā sammadeva agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajanti tadanuttaraṁ—brahmacariyapariyosānaṁ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja vihāsi.
segs.e: Not long after his ordination, Venerable Bhāradvāja, living alone, withdrawn, diligent, keen, and resolute, soon realized the supreme culmination of the spiritual path in this very life. He lived having achieved with his own insight the goal for which gentlemen rightly go forth from the lay life to homelessness.

segs.p: “Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ, kataṁ karaṇīyaṁ, nāparaṁ itthattāyā”ti abbhaññāsi.
segs.e: He understood: “Rebirth is ended; the spiritual journey has been completed; what had to be done has been done; there is nothing further for this place.”

segs.p: Aññataro ca panāyasmā bhāradvājo arahataṁ ahosīti.
segs.e: And Venerable Bhāradvāja became one of the perfected.
Linked Discourses 7.2
1. The Perfected Ones
With Bhāradvāja the Rude

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the squirrels’ feeding ground.
The brahmin Bhāradvāja the Rude heard a rumor that

segs.p: “bhāradvājagotto kira brāhmaṇo samaṇassa gotamassa santike agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajito”ti kupito anattamano yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ asabbhāhi pharusāhi vācāhi akkosati paribhāsati. Evaṁ vutte, bhagavā akkosakabhāradvājaṁ brāhmaṇaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: a brahmin of the Bhāradvāja clan had gone forth from the lay life to homelessness in the presence of the ascetic Gotama. Angry and displeased he went to the Buddha and abused and insulted him with rude, harsh words. When he had spoken, the Buddha said to him:
“What do you think, brahmin?

segs.p: api nu kho te āgacchanti mittāmaccā ñātisālohitā atithiyo”ti?
segs.e: Do friends and colleagues, relatives and kin, and guests still come to visit you?”

segs.p: “Appekadā me, bho gotama, āgacchanti mittāmaccā ñātisālohitā atithiyo”ti.
segs.e: “Sometimes they do, worthy Gotama.”
segs.s: a brahmin of the Bhāradvāja clan

segs.p: “Taṁ kiṁ maññasi, brāhmaṇa, api nu tesaṁ anuppadesi khādanīyaṁ vā bhojanīyaṁ vā sāyanīyaṁ vā”ti?
segs.e: “Do you then serve them with fresh and cooked foods and savories?”

segs.p: “Appekadā nesāhaṁ, bho gotama, anuppademi khādanīyaṁ vā bhojanīyaṁ vā sāyanīyaṁ vā”ti.
segs.e: “Sometimes I do.”
segs.s: a brahmin of the Bhāradvāja clan

segs.p: “Sace kho pana te, brāhmaṇa, nappaṭiggaṇhanti, kassa taṁ hotī”ti?
segs.e: “But if they don’t accept it, brahmin, who does it belong to?”

segs.p: “Sace te, bho gotama, nappaṭiggaṇhanti, amhākameva taṁ hotī”ti.
segs.e: “In that case it still belongs to me.”
segs.s: a brahmin of the Bhāradvāja clan

segs.p: “Evameva kho, brāhmaṇa, yaṁ tvaṁ amhe anakkosante akkosasi, arosente rosesi, abhaṇḍante bhaṇḍasi, taṁ te mayaṁ nappaṭiggaṇhāma.
segs.e: “In the same way, brahmin, when you abuse, harass, and attack us who do not abuse, harass, and attack, we don’t accept it.
It still belongs to you, brahmin,
it still belongs to you!

segs.p: Yo kho, brāhmaṇa, akkosantaṁ paccakkosati, rosentaṁ paṭiroseti, bhaṇḍantaṁ paṭibhaṇḍati, ayaṁ vuccati, brāhmaṇa, sambhuñjati vītiharatīti.
segs.e: Someone who, when abused, harassed, and attacked, abuses, harasses, and attacks in return is said to eat the food and have a reaction to it.

segs.p: Te mayaṁ tayā neva sambhuñjāma na vītiharāma.
segs.e: But we neither eat your food nor do we have a reaction to it.
It still belongs to you, brahmin,
it still belongs to you!”

segs.p: “Bhavantaṁ kho gotamaṁ sarājikā parisā evaṁ jānāti:
segs.e: “The king and his retinue believe of the worthy Gotama,
segs.s: a brahmin of the Bhāradvāja clan

segs.e: ‘the ascetic Gotama is a perfected one’.
segs.s: a brahmin of the Bhāradvāja clan

segs.p: Atha ca pana bhavaṁ gotamo kujjhatī”ti.
segs.e: And yet he still gets angry.”
segs.s: a brahmin of the Bhāradvāja clan

segs.e: “Whence anger for one free of anger,
tamed, living justly,
freed by right knowledge,
peaceful and unaffected?
When you get angry at an angry person
you just make things worse for yourself.
When you don’t get angry at an angry person
you win a battle hard to win.
When you know that the other is angry,
you act for the good of both
yourself and the other
if you’re mindful and stay calm.
People inexpert in the teaching
consider one who heals both
oneself and the other
to be a fool.”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, akkosakabhāradvājo brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When he had spoken, Bhāradvāja the Rude said to the Buddha,
“Excellent, worthy Gotama! …

segs.p: esāhaṁ bhavantaṁ gotamaṁ saraṇaṁ gacchāmi dhammañca bhikkhusaṅghañca.
segs.e: I go for refuge to the worthy Gotama, to the teaching, and to the mendicant Saṅgha.

segs.p: Labheyyāhaṁ, bhante, bhoto gotamassa santike pabbajjaṁ, labheyyaṁ upasampadan”ti.
segs.e: Sir, may I receive the going forth, the ordination in the worthy Gotama’s presence?”

segs.p: Alattha kho akkosakabhāradvājo brāhmaṇo bhagavato santike pabbajjaṁ, alattha upasampadaṁ.
segs.e: And the brahmin Bhāradvāja the Rude received the going forth, the ordination in the Buddha’s presence.

segs.p: Acirūpasampanno kho panāyasmā akkosakabhāradvājo eko vūpakaṭṭho appamatto ātāpī pahitatto viharanto nacirasseva—yassatthāya kulaputtā sammadeva agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajanti tadanuttaraṁ—brahmacariyapariyosānaṁ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja vihāsi.
segs.e: Not long after his ordination, Venerable Bhāradvāja the Rude, living alone, withdrawn, diligent, keen, and resolute, soon realized the supreme culmination of the spiritual path in this very life. He lived having achieved with his own insight the goal for which gentlemen rightly go forth from the lay life to homelessness.

segs.p: “Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ, kataṁ karaṇīyaṁ nāparaṁ itthattāyā”ti abbhaññāsi.
segs.e: He understood: “Rebirth is ended; the spiritual journey has been completed; what had to be done has been done; there is nothing further for this place.”

segs.p: Aññataro ca panāyasmā bhāradvājo arahataṁ ahosīti.
segs.e: And Venerable Bhāradvāja became one of the perfected.
Linked Discourses 7.3
1. The Perfected Ones
With Bhāradvāja the Fiend

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the squirrels’ feeding ground.
The brahmin Bhāradvāja the Fiend heard a rumor to the effect that

segs.p: “bhāradvājagotto brāhmaṇo kira samaṇassa gotamassa santike agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajito”ti kupito anattamano yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ asabbhāhi pharusāhi vācāhi akkosati paribhāsati.
segs.e: a brahmin of the Bhāradvāja clan had gone forth from the lay life to homelessness in the presence of the ascetic Gotama. Angry and displeased he went to the Buddha and abused and insulted him with rude, harsh words.
But when he said this, the Buddha kept silent.

segs.p: Atha kho asurindakabhāradvājo brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Bhāradvāja the Fiend said to the Buddha,
“You’re beaten, ascetic, you’re beaten!”
“‘Ha! I won!’ thinks the fool,
when speaking with harsh words.
The victory for one who understands
is that very endurance.
When you get angry at an angry person
you just make things worse for yourself.
When you don’t get angry at an angry person
you win a battle hard to win.
When you know that the other is angry,
you act for the good of both
yourself and the other
if you’re mindful and stay calm.
People inexpert in Dhamma
consider one who heals both
oneself and the other
to be a fool.”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, asurindakabhāradvājo brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When he had spoken, Bhāradvāja the Fiend said to the Buddha,
“Excellent, worthy Gotama! …” …

segs.p: Aññataro ca panāyasmā bhāradvājo arahataṁ ahosīti.
segs.e: And Venerable Bhāradvāja became one of the perfected.
Linked Discourses 7.4
1. The Perfected Ones
With Bhāradvāja the Bitter

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the squirrels’ feeding ground.
The brahmin Bhāradvāja the Bitter heard a rumor that

segs.p: “bhāradvājagotto kira brāhmaṇo samaṇassa gotamassa santike agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajito”ti kupito anattamano yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā tuṇhībhūto ekamantaṁ aṭṭhāsi.
segs.e: a brahmin of the Bhāradvāja clan had gone forth from the lay life to homelessness in the presence of the ascetic Gotama. Angry and displeased he went to the Buddha and stood silently to one side.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā bilaṅgikassa bhāradvājassa brāhmaṇassa cetasā cetoparivitakkamaññāya bilaṅgikaṁ bhāradvājaṁ brāhmaṇaṁ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi:
segs.e: Then the Buddha, knowing Bhāradvāja the Bitter’s train of thought, addressed him in verse:
“Whoever wrongs a man who has done no wrong,
a pure man who has not a blemish,
the evil backfires on the fool,
like fine dust thrown upwind.”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, bilaṅgikabhāradvājo brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When he said this, the brahmin Bhāradvāja the Bitter said to the Buddha,
“Excellent, worthy Gotama! …” …

segs.p: Aññataro ca panāyasmā bhāradvājo arahataṁ ahosīti.
segs.e: And Venerable Bhāradvāja became one of the perfected.
Linked Discourses 7.5
1. The Perfected Ones
Harmless
At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: Atha kho ahiṁsakabhāradvājo brāhmaṇo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṁ sammodi.
segs.e: Then the brahmin Bhāradvāja the Harmless went up to the Buddha, and exchanged greetings with him.

segs.p: Sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho ahiṁsakabhāradvājo brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side and said,
“I am Harmless, worthy Gotama, I am Harmless!”
“If you were really like your name,
then you’d be Harmless.
But a truly harmless person
does no harm by way of
body, speech, or mind;
they don’t harm anyone else.”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, ahiṁsakabhāradvājo brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When he had spoken, the brahmin Bhāradvāja the Harmless said to the Buddha,
“Excellent, worthy Gotama! …” …

segs.p: Aññataro ca panāyasmā ahiṁsakabhāradvājo arahataṁ ahosīti.
segs.e: And Venerable Bhāradvāja the Harmless became one of the perfected.
Linked Discourses 7.6
1. The Perfected Ones
With Bhāradvāja of the Matted Hair
At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: Atha kho jaṭābhāradvājo brāhmaṇo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṁ sammodi.
segs.e: Then the brahmin Bhāradvāja of the Matted Hair went up to the Buddha, and exchanged greetings with him.

segs.p: Sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi.
segs.e: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side,

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho jaṭābhāradvājo brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṁ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi:
segs.e: and addressed the Buddha in verse:
“Tangled within, tangled without:
segs.s: the brahmin Bhāradvāja of the Matted Hair

segs.e: these people are tangled in tangles.
segs.s: the brahmin Bhāradvāja of the Matted Hair

segs.e: I ask you this, Gotama:
segs.s: the brahmin Bhāradvāja of the Matted Hair

segs.e: who can untangle this tangle?”
segs.s: the brahmin Bhāradvāja of the Matted Hair

segs.e: “A wise person grounded in ethics,
developing the mind and wisdom,
a keen and alert mendicant—
they can untangle this tangle.
Those in whom greed, hate, and ignorance
have faded away;
the perfected ones with defilements ended—
they have untangled the tangle.
Where name and form
cease with no residue left behind;
as well as impingement and perception of form:
it’s here this tangle is cut.”
When he had spoken, Bhāradvāja of the Matted Hair said to the Buddha,
“Excellent, worthy Gotama! …” …

segs.p: aññataro ca panāyasmā bhāradvājo arahataṁ ahosī”ti.
segs.e: And Venerable Bhāradvāja became one of the perfected.
Linked Discourses 7.7
1. The Perfected Ones
With Bhāradvāja the Pure
At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: Atha kho suddhikabhāradvājo brāhmaṇo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṁ sammodi.
segs.e: Then the brahmin Bhāradvāja the Pure went up to the Buddha, and exchanged greetings with him.

segs.p: Sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi.
segs.e: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side,

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho suddhikabhāradvājo brāhmaṇo bhagavato santike imaṁ gāthaṁ ajjhabhāsi:
segs.e: and spoke this verse in his presence:
“No brahmin in the world is ever purified
even though he’s ethical and mortifies himself.
But one accomplished in knowledge and conduct

segs.p: So sujjhati na aññā itarā pajā”ti.
segs.e: is purified, not these other commoners.”
“Even one who mutters many prayers
is no brahmin by birth
if they’re filthy and corrupt within,
supporting themselves by fawning.
Regardless of whether you’re an aristocrat,
a brahmin, peasant, menial, <j>or a corpse-worker or scavenger—
if you’re energetic and resolute,
always staunchly vigorous,
you’ll attain ultimate purity.
Know that for a fact, brahmin.”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, suddhikabhāradvājo brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When he had spoken, the brahmin Bhāradvāja the Pure said to the Buddha,
“Excellent, worthy Gotama …” …

segs.p: aññataro ca panāyasmā bhāradvājo arahataṁ ahosīti.
segs.e: And Venerable Bhāradvāja became one of the perfected.
Linked Discourses 7.8
1. The Perfected Ones
With Bhāradvāja the Fire-Worshiper

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the squirrels’ feeding ground.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena aggikabhāradvājassa brāhmaṇassa sappinā pāyaso sannihito hoti:
segs.e: Now at that time ghee and milk-rice had been set out for the brahmin Bhāradvāja the Fire-Worshiper, who thought,
“I will serve the sacred flame! I will perform the fire sacrifice!”

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā pubbaṇhasamayaṁ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya rājagahaṁ piṇḍāya pāvisi.
segs.e: Then the Buddha robed up in the morning and, taking his bowl and robe, entered Rājagaha for alms.

segs.p: Rājagahe sapadānaṁ piṇḍāya caramāno yena aggikabhāradvājassa brāhmaṇassa nivesanaṁ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā ekamantaṁ aṭṭhāsi.
segs.e: Wandering indiscriminately for almsfood in Rājagaha, he approached Bhāradvāja the Fire-Worshiper’s home and stood to one side.

segs.p: Addasā kho aggikabhāradvājo brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṁ piṇḍāya ṭhitaṁ.
segs.e: Bhāradvāja the Fire-Worshiper saw him standing for alms
and addressed him in verse:
“One who’s accomplished in the three knowledges,
of good birth and ample learning,
accomplished in knowledge and conduct
may enjoy this milk-rice.”
“Even one who mutters many prayers
is no brahmin by birth
if they’re filthy and corrupt within,
with a following gained by fawning.
One who knows their past lives,
sees heaven and places of loss,
and has attained the ending of rebirth,
is a sage of perfect insight.
Because of these three knowledges
a brahmin is a master of the three knowledges.
Accomplished in knowledge and conduct,
they may enjoy this milk-rice.”
“May the worthy Gotama eat!
The worthy one is a brahmin.”
“Food enchanted by a verse isn’t fit for me to eat.
That’s not the principle of those who see, brahmin.
The Buddhas cast aside things enchanted with verses.
Since there is such a principle, brahmin, <j>that’s how they live.
Serve with other food and drink
the consummate one, the great seer,
with defilements ended and remorse stilled.
For he is the field for the seeker of merit.”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, aggikabhāradvājo brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When he had spoken, the brahmin Bhāradvāja the Fire-Worshiper said to the Buddha,
“Excellent, worthy Gotama! …” …

segs.p: aññataro ca panāyasmā aggikabhāradvājo arahataṁ ahosīti.
segs.e: And Venerable Bhāradvāja the Fire-Worshiper became one of the perfected.
Linked Discourses 7.9
1. The Perfected Ones
With Bhāradvāja of Sundarikā

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā kosalesu viharati sundarikāya nadiyā tīre.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying in the Kosalan lands on the bank of the Sundarikā River.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena sundarikabhāradvājo brāhmaṇo sundarikāya nadiyā tīre aggiṁ juhati, aggihuttaṁ paricarati.
segs.e: Now at that time the brahmin Bhāradvāja of Sundarikā was serving the sacred flame and performing the fire sacrifice on the bank of the Sundarikā.

segs.p: Atha kho sundarikabhāradvājo brāhmaṇo aggiṁ juhitvā aggihuttaṁ paricaritvā uṭṭhāyāsanā samantā catuddisā anuvilokesi:
segs.e: Then he rose from his seat and surveyed the four quarters, wondering,
“Now who might eat the leftovers of this oblation?”

segs.p: Addasā kho sundarikabhāradvājo brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṁ aññatarasmiṁ rukkhamūle sasīsaṁ pārutaṁ nisinnaṁ.
segs.e: He saw the Buddha meditating at the root of a certain tree with his robe pulled over his head.

segs.p: Disvāna vāmena hatthena habyasesaṁ gahetvā dakkhiṇena hatthena kamaṇḍaluṁ gahetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami.
segs.e: Taking the leftovers of the oblation in his left hand and a pitcher in the right he approached the Buddha.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā sundarikabhāradvājassa brāhmaṇassa padasaddena sīsaṁ vivari.
segs.e: When he heard Bhāradvāja of Sundarikā’s footsteps the Buddha uncovered his head.

segs.p: Atha kho sundarikabhāradvājo brāhmaṇo “muṇḍo ayaṁ bhavaṁ, muṇḍako ayaṁ bhavan”ti tatova puna nivattitukāmo ahosi.
segs.e: Bhāradvāja of Sundarikā thought, “This man is shaven, he is shaven!” And he wanted to turn back.
But he thought,
“Even some brahmins are shaven.
Why don’t I go to him and ask about his birth?”

segs.p: Atha kho sundarikabhāradvājo brāhmaṇo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then the brahmin Bhāradvāja of Sundarikā went up to the Buddha, and said to him,
“Sir, what are you by birth?”
“Don’t ask about birth, ask about conduct;
for the fire of Jātaveda is born from sticks.
A steadfast sage, even though from a low class family,
is a thoroughbred checked by conscience.
Tamed by truth, fulfilled by taming,
a complete knowledge master <j>who has completed the spiritual journey—
that’s who a sacrificer should woo,
and offer a timely oblation <j>to one worthy of a religious donation.”
“My sacrificial offering <j>must have been well performed,
since I have met such a knowledge master!
It’s because I’d never met anyone like you
that others ate the leftover oblation.
May the worthy Gotama eat!
The worthy one is a brahmin.”
“Food enchanted by a verse isn’t fit for me to eat.
That’s not the principle of those who see, brahmin.
The Buddhas cast aside things enchanted with verses.
Since there is such a principle, brahmin, <j>that’s how they live.
Serve with other food and drink
the consummate one, the great seer,
with defilements ended and remorse stilled.
For he is the field for the seeker of merit.”

segs.p: “Atha kassa cāhaṁ, bho gotama, imaṁ habyasesaṁ dammī”ti?
segs.e: “Then, Worthy Gotama, to whom should I give the leftovers of this oblation?”

segs.p: “Na khvāhaṁ, brāhmaṇa, passāmi sadevake loke samārake sabrahmake sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiyā pajāya sadevamanussāya yasseso habyaseso bhutto sammā pariṇāmaṁ gaccheyya aññatra, brāhmaṇa, tathāgatassa vā tathāgatasāvakassa vā.
segs.e: “Brahmin, I don’t see anyone in this world—with its gods, Māras, and divinities, this population with its ascetics and brahmins, its gods and humans—who can properly digest these leftovers, except the Realized One or one of his disciples.

segs.p: Tena hi tvaṁ, brāhmaṇa, taṁ habyasesaṁ appaharite vā chaḍḍehi appāṇake vā udake opilāpehī”ti.
segs.e: Well then, brahmin, throw out those leftovers where there is little that grows, or drop them into water that has no living creatures.”

segs.p: Atha kho sundarikabhāradvājo brāhmaṇo taṁ habyasesaṁ appāṇake udake opilāpesi.
segs.e: So Bhāradvāja of Sundarikā dropped the leftover oblation in water that had no living creatures.

segs.p: Atha kho so habyaseso udake pakkhitto cicciṭāyati ciṭiciṭāyati sandhūpāyati sampadhūpāyati.
segs.e: And when those leftovers were placed in the water, they sizzled and hissed, steaming and fuming.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi nāma phālo divasaṁsantatto udake pakkhitto cicciṭāyati ciṭiciṭāyati sandhūpāyati sampadhūpāyati;
segs.e: Suppose there was an iron cauldron that had been heated all day. If you placed it in the water, it would sizzle and hiss, steaming and fuming.

segs.p: evameva so habyaseso udake pakkhitto cicciṭāyati ciṭiciṭāyati sandhūpāyati sampadhūpāyati.
segs.e: In the same way, when those leftovers were placed in the water, they sizzled and hissed, steaming and fuming.

segs.p: Atha kho sundarikabhāradvājo brāhmaṇo saṁviggo lomahaṭṭhajāto yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā ekamantaṁ aṭṭhāsi.
segs.e: Then the brahmin Bhāradvāja of Sundarikā, shocked and awestruck, went up to the Buddha, and stood to one side.

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ ṭhitaṁ kho sundarikabhāradvājaṁ brāhmaṇaṁ bhagavā gāthāhi ajjhabhāsi:
segs.e: The Buddha addressed him in verse:
“When you’re kindling the wood, brahmin,
don’t imagine this is purity, for it’s just external.

segs.p: Na hi tena suddhiṁ kusalā vadanti,
segs.e: For those who are skilled say this is no way to purity,
when one seeks purity in externals.
I’ve given up kindling firewood, brahmin,
now I light only the inner flame.
Always blazing, always serene,
I am a perfected one leading the spiritual life.
Conceit, brahmin, is the burden of your pack,
anger your smoke, and lies your ashes.
The tongue is the ladle, the heart the fireplace;
a well-tamed self is a person’s light.
The teaching is a lake, brahmin, <j>into which ethics are the stairs,
unclouded, praised by the fine to the good.
There the knowledge masters go to bathe,
and cross to the far shore with dry limbs.
Truth, principle, restraint, the spiritual life,
attaining divinity based on the middle, brahmin—
pay homage to the upright ones.
I declare that man one who follows the teaching.”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, sundarikabhāradvājo brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When he had spoken, the brahmin Bhāradvāja of Sundarikā said to the Buddha,
“Excellent, worthy Gotama …” …

segs.p: aññataro ca panāyasmā bhāradvājo arahataṁ ahosīti.
segs.e: And Venerable Bhāradvāja became one of the perfected.
Linked Discourses 7.10
1. The Perfected Ones
Many Daughters

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā kosalesu viharati aññatarasmiṁ vanasaṇḍe.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying in the land of the Kosalans in a certain forest grove.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena aññatarassa bhāradvājagottassa brāhmaṇassa catuddasa balībaddā naṭṭhā honti.
segs.e: Now at that time one of the brahmins of the Bhāradvāja clan had lost fourteen oxen.

segs.p: Atha kho bhāradvājagotto brāhmaṇo te balībadde gavesanto yena so vanasaṇḍo tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā addasa bhagavantaṁ tasmiṁ vanasaṇḍe nisinnaṁ pallaṅkaṁ ābhujitvā ujuṁ kāyaṁ paṇidhāya parimukhaṁ satiṁ upaṭṭhapetvā.
segs.e: While looking for them he went to that forest grove, where he saw the Buddha sitting down cross-legged, his body set straight, and mindfulness brought to the present.

segs.p: Disvāna yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavato santike imā gāthāyo abhāsi:
segs.e: He went up to the Buddha, and recited these verses in the Buddha’s presence:
“This ascetic mustn’t have
fourteen oxen
missing for the past six days:
that’s why this ascetic is happy.
This ascetic mustn’t have
a field of sesame ruined,
with just one or two leaves:
that’s why this ascetic is happy.
This ascetic mustn’t have
rats in a vacant barn
dancing merrily:
that’s why this ascetic is happy.
This ascetic mustn’t have
carpets that for seven months
have been infested with fleas:
that’s why this ascetic is happy.
This ascetic mustn’t have
seven widowed daughters
with one or two children each:
that’s why this ascetic is happy.
This ascetic mustn’t have
a wife with sallow, blotchy skin
to wake him with a kick:
that’s why this ascetic is happy.
This ascetic mustn’t have
creditors knocking at dawn,
demanding, ‘Pay up! Pay up!’:
that’s why this ascetic is happy.”
“You’re right, brahmin, I don’t have
fourteen oxen
missing for the past six days:
that’s why I’m happy, brahmin.
You’re right, brahmin, I don’t have
a field of sesame ruined,
with just one or two leaves:
that’s why I’m happy, brahmin.
You’re right, brahmin, I don’t have
rats in a vacant barn
dancing merrily:
that’s why I’m happy, brahmin.
You’re right, brahmin, I don’t have
carpets that for seven months
have been infested with fleas:
that’s why I’m happy, brahmin.
You’re right, brahmin, I don’t have
seven widowed daughters
with one or two children each:
that’s why I’m happy, brahmin.
You’re right, brahmin, I don’t have
a wife with blotchy, pockmarked skin
to wake me up with a kick:
that’s why I’m happy, brahmin.
You’re right, brahmin, I don’t have
creditors knocking at dawn,
warning, ‘Pay up! Pay up!’:
that’s why I’m happy, brahmin.”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, bhāradvājagotto brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When he had spoken, the brahmin said to the Buddha,
“Excellent, worthy Gotama! Excellent! …

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bho gotama, nikkujjitaṁ vā ukkujjeyya, paṭicchannaṁ vā vivareyya, mūḷhassa vā maggaṁ ācikkheyya, andhakāre vā telapajjotaṁ dhāreyya: ‘cakkhumanto rūpāni dakkhantī’ti; evameva bhotā gotamena anekapariyāyena dhammo pakāsito.
segs.e: As if he were righting the overturned, or revealing the hidden, or pointing out the path to the lost, or lighting a lamp in the dark so people with clear eyes can see what’s there, worthy Gotama has made the teaching clear in many ways.

segs.p: Esāhaṁ bhavantaṁ gotamaṁ saraṇaṁ gacchāmi dhammañca bhikkhusaṅghañca.
segs.e: I go for refuge to the worthy Gotama, to the teaching, and to the mendicant Saṅgha.

segs.p: Labheyyāhaṁ bhoto gotamassa santike pabbajjaṁ, labheyyaṁ upasampadan”ti.
segs.e: May I receive the going forth, the ordination in the worthy Gotama’s presence?”

segs.p: Alattha kho bhāradvājagotto brāhmaṇo bhagavato santike pabbajjaṁ, alattha upasampadaṁ.
segs.e: And the brahmin received the going forth, the ordination in the Buddha’s presence.

segs.p: Acirūpasampanno panāyasmā bhāradvājo eko vūpakaṭṭho appamatto ātāpī pahitatto viharanto nacirasseva—yassatthāya kulaputtā sammadeva agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajanti, tadanuttaraṁ—brahmacariyapariyosānaṁ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja vihāsi.
segs.e: Not long after his ordination, Venerable Bhāradvāja, living alone, withdrawn, diligent, keen, and resolute, soon realized the supreme culmination of the spiritual path in this very life. He lived having achieved with his own insight the goal for which gentlemen rightly go forth from the lay life to homelessness.

segs.p: “Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ, kataṁ karaṇīyaṁ, nāparaṁ itthattāyā”ti abbhaññāsi.
segs.e: He understood: “Rebirth is ended; the spiritual journey has been completed; what had to be done has been done; there is nothing further for this place.”

segs.p: Aññataro ca panāyasmā bhāradvājo arahataṁ ahosīti.
segs.e: And Venerable Bhāradvāja became one of the perfected.
Linked Discourses 7.11
2. Lay Followers
With Bhāradvāja the Farmer
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā magadhesu viharati dakkhiṇāgirismiṁ ekanāḷāyaṁ brāhmaṇagāme.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying in the land of the Magadhans in the Southern Hills near the brahmin village of Ekanāḷa.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena kasibhāradvājassa brāhmaṇassa pañcamattāni naṅgalasatāni payuttāni honti vappakāle.
segs.e: Now at that time the brahmin Bhāradvāja the Farmer had harnessed around five hundred plows, it being the season for sowing.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā pubbaṇhasamayaṁ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya yena kasibhāradvājassa brāhmaṇassa kammanto tenupasaṅkami.
segs.e: Then the Buddha robed up in the morning and, taking his bowl and robe, went to where Bhāradvāja the Farmer was working.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena kasibhāradvājassa brāhmaṇassa parivesanā vattati.
segs.e: Now at that time Bhāradvāja the Farmer was distributing food.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā yena parivesanā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā ekamantaṁ aṭṭhāsi.
segs.e: Then the Buddha went to where the distribution was taking place and stood to one side.

segs.p: Addasā kho kasibhāradvājo brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṁ piṇḍāya ṭhitaṁ.
segs.e: Bhāradvāja the Farmer saw him standing for alms
and said to him,

segs.p: “ahaṁ kho, samaṇa, kasāmi ca vapāmi ca, kasitvā ca vapitvā ca bhuñjāmi.
segs.e: “I plough and sow, ascetic, and then I eat.

segs.p: Tvampi, samaṇa, kasassu ca vapassu ca, kasitvā ca vapitvā ca bhuñjassū”ti.
segs.e: You too should plough and sow, then you may eat.”

segs.p: “Ahampi kho, brāhmaṇa, kasāmi ca vapāmi ca, kasitvā ca vapitvā ca bhuñjāmī”ti.
segs.e: “I too plough and sow, brahmin, and then I eat.”

segs.p: “Na kho mayaṁ passāma bhoto gotamassa yugaṁ vā naṅgalaṁ vā phālaṁ vā pācanaṁ vā balībadde vā, atha ca pana bhavaṁ gotamo evamāha:
segs.e: “I don’t see the worthy Gotama with a yoke or plow or plowshare or goad or oxen, yet he says:

segs.p: ‘ahampi kho, brāhmaṇa, kasāmi ca vapāmi ca, kasitvā ca vapitvā ca bhuñjāmī’”ti.
segs.e: ‘I too plough and sow, brahmin, and then I eat.’”

segs.p: Atha kho kasibhāradvājo brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṁ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi:
segs.e: Then Bhāradvāja the Farmer addressed the Buddha in verse:
“You claim to be a farmer,
but I don’t see you farming.
Tell me how you’re a farmer when asked:
how am I to recognize your farming?”
“Faith is my seed, fervor my rain,
and wisdom is my yoke and plough.
Conscience is my draft-pole, mind my strap,
mindfulness my plowshare and goad.
Guarded in body and speech,
I restrict my intake of food.
I use truth as my scythe,
and gentleness is my release.
Energy is my harnessed beast,
transporting me to sanctuary from the yoke.
Without turning back, it goes
to where there is no sorrow.
That’s how to do the farming
that has freedom from death as its fruit.
When you finish this farming
you’re released from all suffering.”
“May the worthy Gotama eat!
The worthy one is a farmer.

segs.p: Yañhi bhavaṁ gotamo amatapphalampi kasiṁ kasatī”ti.
segs.e: For the worthy Gotama does the farming that has freedom from death as its fruit.”
“Food enchanted by a verse isn’t fit for me to eat.
That’s not the principle of those who see, brahmin.
The Buddhas cast aside things enchanted with verses.
Since there is such a principle, brahmin, <j>that’s how they live.
Serve with other food and drink
the consummate one, the great seer,
with defilements ended and remorse stilled.
For he is the field for the seeker of merit.”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, kasibhāradvājo brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When he had spoken, the brahmin Bhāradvāja the Farmer said to the Buddha,
“Excellent, worthy Gotama …
From this day forth, may the worthy Gotama remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.”
Linked Discourses 7.12
2. Lay Followers
With Udaya
At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā pubbaṇhasamayaṁ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya yena udayassa brāhmaṇassa nivesanaṁ tenupasaṅkami.
segs.e: Then the Buddha robed up in the morning and, taking his bowl and robe, went to the home of the brahmin Udaya.

segs.p: Atha kho udayo brāhmaṇo bhagavato pattaṁ odanena pūresi.
segs.e: Then Udaya filled the Buddha’s bowl with rice.

segs.p: Dutiyampi kho bhagavā pubbaṇhasamayaṁ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya yena udayassa brāhmaṇassa nivesanaṁ tenupasaṅkami …pe…
segs.e: The next day … Udaya again filled the Buddha’s bowl with rice.

segs.p: tatiyampi kho udayo brāhmaṇo bhagavato pattaṁ odanena pūretvā bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: But when he had filled the Buddha’s bowl on the third day, he said to the Buddha,
“This ascetic Gotama is such a drag! He keeps coming back again and again!”
“Again and again, they sow the seed;
again and again, the king of the heavens sends rain;
again and again, farmers plough the field;
again and again, grain is produced for the nation.
Again and again, the beggars beg;
again and again, the donors give.
Again and again, when the donors have given,
again and again, they take their place in heaven.
Again and again, dairy farmers milk;
again and again, a calf cleaves to its mother;
again and again, oppressing and intimidating,
that dullard returns to the womb again and again.
Again and again, you’re reborn and die;
again and again, you get carried to a charnel ground.
But when they’ve gained the path <j>for no further rebirth,
one of vast wisdom is not reborn again and again.”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, udayo brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When he had spoken, the brahmin Udaya said to the Buddha,
“Excellent, worthy Gotama …

segs.p: upāsakaṁ maṁ bhavaṁ gotamo dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṁ saraṇaṁ gatan”ti.
segs.e: From this day forth, may the worthy Gotama remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.”
Linked Discourses 7.13
2. Lay Followers
With Devahita
At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena bhagavā vātehābādhiko hoti;
segs.e: Now at that time the Buddha was afflicted by winds.

segs.p: āyasmā ca upavāṇo bhagavato upaṭṭhāko hoti.
segs.e: Venerable Upavāṇa was his carer.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā āyasmantaṁ upavāṇaṁ āmantesi:
segs.e: Then the Buddha said to Upavāṇa,
“Go on then, Upavāṇa, find some hot water for me.”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bhante”ti kho āyasmā upavāṇo bhagavato paṭissutvā nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya yena devahitassa brāhmaṇassa nivesanaṁ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā tuṇhībhūto ekamantaṁ aṭṭhāsi.
segs.e: “Yes, sir,” replied Upavāṇa. He robed up, and, taking his bowl and robe, went to the home of the brahmin Devahita, and stood silently to one side.

segs.p: Addasā kho devahito brāhmaṇo āyasmantaṁ upavāṇaṁ tuṇhībhūtaṁ ekamantaṁ ṭhitaṁ.
segs.e: Devahita saw him standing there
and addressed him in verse:
“Silent stands the worthy one,
shaven, wrapped in his outer robe.
What do you want? What are you looking for?
What have you come here to ask for?”
“The perfected one, the Holy One in the world,
the sage is afflicted by winds.
If there’s hot water,
give it to the sage, brahmin.
I wish to bring it to the one
who is esteemed by the estimable,
honored by the honorable,
venerated by the venerable.”

segs.p: Atha kho devahito brāhmaṇo uṇhodakassa kājaṁ purisena gāhāpetvā phāṇitassa ca puṭaṁ āyasmato upavāṇassa pādāsi.
segs.e: Then Devahita had a man fetch a carrying-pole with hot water. He also presented Upavāṇa with a jar of molasses.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā upavāṇo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ uṇhodakena nhāpetvā uṇhodakena phāṇitaṁ āloletvā bhagavato pādāsi.
segs.e: Then Venerable Upavāṇa went up to the Buddha and bathed him with the hot water. Then he stirred molasses into hot water and presented it to the Buddha.
Then the Buddha’s illness died down.

segs.p: Atha kho devahito brāhmaṇo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṁ sammodi.
segs.e: Then the brahmin Devahita went up to the Buddha, and exchanged greetings with him.

segs.p: Sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi.
segs.e: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side,

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho devahito brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṁ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi:
segs.e: and addressed the Buddha in verse:
“Where should you give an available gift?
Where is a gift very fruitful?
How does one who is donating
ensure the success of their religious donation?”
“One who knows their past lives,
sees heaven and places of loss,
and has attained the ending of rebirth,
is a sage of perfect insight.
Here you should give an available gift;
what’s given here is very fruitful.
That’s how a sponsor of sacrifices
ensures the success of their religious donation.”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, devahito brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When he had spoken, the brahmin Devahita said to the Buddha,
“Excellent, worthy Gotama …

segs.p: upāsakaṁ maṁ bhavaṁ gotamo dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṁ saraṇaṁ gatan”ti.
segs.e: From this day forth, may the worthy Gotama remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.”
Linked Discourses 7.14
2. Lay Followers
A well-to-do brahmin
At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: Atha kho aññataro brāhmaṇamahāsālo lūkho lūkhapāvuraṇo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṁ sammodi.
segs.e: Then a certain well-to-do brahmin, shabby, wearing a shabby cloak, went up to the Buddha, and exchanged greetings with him.

segs.p: Sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho taṁ brāhmaṇamahāsālaṁ bhagavā etadavoca:
segs.e: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side. The Buddha said to him,
“Brahmin, why are you so shabby, wearing a shabby cloak?”
“Worthy Gotama, I have four sons.

segs.p: Te maṁ dārehi sampuccha gharā nikkhāmentī”ti.
segs.e: At their wives’ bidding they expelled me from my house.”

segs.p: “Tena hi tvaṁ, brāhmaṇa, imā gāthāyo pariyāpuṇitvā sabhāyaṁ mahājanakāye sannipatite puttesu ca sannisinnesu bhāsassu:
segs.e: “Well then, brahmin, memorize these verses and recite them to your sons when you are all seated in the council hall with a large crowd.
‘I was overjoyed when they were born,
and wished prosperity for them.
But at their wives’ bidding they chased me out,
like hounds after hogs.
It turns out they’re wicked, those nasty men,
though they called me their dear old Dad.
They’re monsters in the shape of sons,
throwing me out as I’ve grown old.
Like an old, useless horse
led away from its fodder,
the elderly father of those kids
begs for alms at others’ homes.
Even my staff is better
than those disobedient sons,
for it wards off a wild bull,
and even a wild dog.
It goes before me in the dark;
in deep waters it finds a footing.
By the wonderful power of this staff,
when I stumble, I stand firm again.’”

segs.p: Atha kho so brāhmaṇamahāsālo bhagavato santike imā gāthāyo pariyāpuṇitvā sabhāyaṁ mahājanakāye sannipatite puttesu ca sannisinnesu abhāsi:
segs.e: Having memorized those verses in the Buddha’s presence, the brahmin recited them to his sons when they were all seated in the council hall with a large crowd. …

segs.p: Atha kho naṁ brāhmaṇamahāsālaṁ puttā gharaṁ netvā nhāpetvā paccekaṁ dussayugena acchādesuṁ.
segs.e: Then the brahmin’s sons led him back home, bathed him, and each clothed him with a fine pair of garments.

segs.p: Atha kho so brāhmaṇamahāsālo ekaṁ dussayugaṁ ādāya yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṁ sammodi.
segs.e: Then the brahmin, taking one pair of garments, went to the Buddha and exchanged greetings with him.

segs.p: Sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho brāhmaṇamahāsālo bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side and said to the Buddha:

segs.p: “mayaṁ, bho gotama, brāhmaṇā nāma ācariyassa ācariyadhanaṁ pariyesāma.
segs.e: “Worthy Gotama, we brahmins seek a fee for our tutor.
May the worthy Gotama please accept my tutor’s fee!”
So the Buddha accepted it out of sympathy.

segs.p: Atha kho so brāhmaṇamahāsālo bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then the well-to-do brahmin said to the Buddha,
“Excellent, worthy Gotama …

segs.p: upāsakaṁ maṁ bhavaṁ gotamo dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṁ saraṇaṁ gatan”ti.
segs.e: From this day forth, may the worthy Gotama remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.”
Linked Discourses 7.15
2. Lay Followers
Stuck-Up
At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena mānatthaddho nāma brāhmaṇo sāvatthiyaṁ paṭivasati.
segs.e: Now at that time a brahmin named Stuck-Up was residing in Sāvatthī.

segs.p: So neva mātaraṁ abhivādeti, na pitaraṁ abhivādeti, na ācariyaṁ abhivādeti, na jeṭṭhabhātaraṁ abhivādeti.
segs.e: He didn’t bow to his mother or father, his tutor, or his oldest brother.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena bhagavā mahatiyā parisāya parivuto dhammaṁ deseti.
segs.e: Now, at that time the Buddha was teaching Dhamma, surrounded by a large assembly.
Then Stuck-Up thought,

segs.p: “ayaṁ kho samaṇo gotamo mahatiyā parisāya parivuto dhammaṁ deseti.
segs.e: “The ascetic Gotama is teaching Dhamma, surrounded by a large assembly.
Why don’t I approach him?

segs.p: Sace maṁ samaṇo gotamo ālapissati, ahampi taṁ ālapissāmi.
segs.e: If he speaks to me, I’ll speak to him.

segs.p: No ce maṁ samaṇo gotamo ālapissati, ahampi nālapissāmī”ti.
segs.e: But if he doesn’t speak, neither will I.”

segs.p: Atha kho mānatthaddho brāhmaṇo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā tuṇhībhūto ekamantaṁ aṭṭhāsi.
segs.e: Then the brahmin Stuck-Up went up to the Buddha, and stood silently to one side.
But the Buddha didn’t speak to him.
Then Stuck-Up thought,

segs.p: “nāyaṁ samaṇo gotamo kiñci jānātī”ti tatova puna nivattitukāmo ahosi.
segs.e: “This ascetic Gotama knows nothing!” And he wanted to go back from there right away.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā mānatthaddhassa brāhmaṇassa cetasā cetoparivitakkamaññāya mānatthaddhaṁ brāhmaṇaṁ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi:
segs.e: Then the Buddha, knowing Stuck-Up’s train of thought, addressed him in verse:
“It’s not good to foster conceit
if you want what’s good for you, brahmin.
You should foster the goal
which brought you here.”
Then Stuck-Up thought,

segs.p: “cittaṁ me samaṇo gotamo jānātī”ti tattheva bhagavato pādesu sirasā nipatitvā bhagavato pādāni mukhena ca paricumbati pāṇīhi ca parisambāhati, nāmañca sāveti:
segs.e: “The ascetic Gotama knows my mind!” He bowed with his head to the Buddha’s feet, caressing them and covering them with kisses, and pronounced his name:
“Worthy Gotama, I am Stuck-Up! I am Stuck-Up!”

segs.p: Atha kho sā parisā abbhutavittajātā ahosi:
segs.e: Then that assembly was stunned:
“Oh lord, how incredible, how amazing!

segs.p: Ayañhi mānatthaddho brāhmaṇo neva mātaraṁ abhivādeti, na pitaraṁ abhivādeti, na ācariyaṁ abhivādeti, na jeṭṭhabhātaraṁ abhivādeti;
segs.e: This brahmin Stuck-Up doesn’t bow to his mother or father, his tutor, or his oldest brother.

segs.p: atha ca pana samaṇe gotame evarūpaṁ paramanipaccakāraṁ karotī”ti.
segs.e: Yet he shows such utmost deference to the ascetic Gotama!”

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā mānatthaddhaṁ brāhmaṇaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then the Buddha said to the brahmin Stuck-Up,
“Enough, brahmin. Get up, and take your own seat.
For your mind has confidence in me.”

segs.p: Atha kho mānatthaddho brāhmaṇo sake āsane nisīditvā bhagavantaṁ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi:
segs.e: Then Stuck-Up took his seat and said to the Buddha:
“Regarding whom should you not be conceited?
Who should you respect?
Who should you esteem?
Who is it good to venerate properly?”
“Your mother and father,
and also your oldest brother,
with tutor as fourth.
Regarding these you should not be conceited.
They are who you should respect.
They are who you should esteem.
And they’re who it’s good to venerate properly.
And when with bent knee, not stiff with conceit,
show supreme reverence for
the perfected ones—cooled,
their task complete, free of defilements.”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, mānatthaddho brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When he had spoken, the brahmin Stuck-Up said to the Buddha,
“Excellent, worthy Gotama …

segs.p: upāsakaṁ maṁ bhavaṁ gotamo dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṁ saraṇaṁ gatan”ti.
segs.e: From this day forth, may the worthy Gotama remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.”
Linked Discourses 7.16
2. Lay Followers
The Contraphile
At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena paccanīkasāto nāma brāhmaṇo sāvatthiyaṁ paṭivasati.
segs.e: Now at that time a brahmin named Contraphile, who loved contradiction, was residing in Sāvatthī.
Then Contraphile thought,
“Why don’t I go to the ascetic Gotama and

segs.p: Yaṁ yadeva samaṇo gotamo bhāsissati taṁ tadevassāhaṁ paccanīkāssan”ti.
segs.e: contradict everything he says?”

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena bhagavā abbhokāse caṅkamati.
segs.e: At that time the Buddha was walking mindfully in the open air.

segs.p: Atha kho paccanīkasāto brāhmaṇo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ caṅkamantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then the brahmin Contraphile went up to the Buddha, and said to him as he was walking,
“Ascetic, preach the Dhamma.”
“Fine words aren’t easy to understand
by a lover of contradiction,
whose mind is tainted
and full of aggression.
But when you’ve dispelled aggression,
and your suspicious mind,
and you’ve got rid of resentment,
then you’ll understand fine words.”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, paccanīkasāto brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When he had spoken, the brahmin Contraphile said to the Buddha,
“Excellent, worthy Gotama! Excellent! …

segs.p: upāsakaṁ maṁ bhavaṁ gotamo dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṁ saraṇaṁ gatan”ti.
segs.e: From this day forth, may the worthy Gotama remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.”
Linked Discourses 7.17
2. Lay Followers
The Builder

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā kosalesu viharati aññatarasmiṁ vanasaṇḍe.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying in the land of the Kosalans in a certain forest grove.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena navakammikabhāradvājo brāhmaṇo tasmiṁ vanasaṇḍe kammantaṁ kārāpeti.
segs.e: Now at that time the brahmin Bhāradvāja the Builder was having some building work done in that jungle thicket.

segs.p: Addasā kho navakammikabhāradvājo brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṁ aññatarasmiṁ sālarukkhamūle nisinnaṁ pallaṅkaṁ ābhujitvā ujuṁ kāyaṁ paṇidhāya parimukhaṁ satiṁ upaṭṭhapetvā.
segs.e: He saw the Buddha sitting down cross-legged at the root of a certain sal tree, his body set straight, and mindfulness brought to the present.
Seeing this, it occurred to him,

segs.p: “ahaṁ kho imasmiṁ vanasaṇḍe kammantaṁ kārāpento ramāmi.
segs.e: “I enjoy having this building work done here in the jungle.

segs.p: Ayaṁ samaṇo gotamo kiṁ kārāpento ramatī”ti?
segs.e: I wonder what the ascetic Gotama enjoys having done?”

segs.p: Atha kho navakammikabhāradvājo brāhmaṇo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami. upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi:
segs.e: Then Bhāradvāja the Builder went up to the Buddha and addressed him in verse:
“What kind of works are done by you,
a mendicant in the sal jungle?
How do you find enjoyment
alone in the wilderness, Gotama?”
“There’s nothing I need do in the jungle;
my jungle’s cut at the root, it’s withered away.
Free of snarls and thorns in the jungle,
I enjoy solitude, having given up discontent.”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, navakammikabhāradvājo brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When he had spoken, the brahmin Bhāradvāja the Builder said to the Buddha,
“Excellent, worthy Gotama …

segs.p: upāsakaṁ maṁ bhavaṁ gotamo dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṁ saraṇaṁ gatan”ti.
segs.e: From this day forth, may the worthy Gotama remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.”
Linked Discourses 7.18
2. Lay Followers
Collecting Firewood

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā kosalesu viharati aññatarasmiṁ vanasaṇḍe.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying in the land of the Kosalans in a certain forest grove.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena aññatarassa bhāradvājagottassa brāhmaṇassa sambahulā antevāsikā kaṭṭhahārakā māṇavakā yena vanasaṇḍo tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā addasaṁsu bhagavantaṁ tasmiṁ vanasaṇḍe nisinnaṁ pallaṅkaṁ ābhujitvā ujuṁ kāyaṁ paṇidhāya parimukhaṁ satiṁ upaṭṭhapetvā. Disvāna yena bhāradvājagotto brāhmaṇo tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhāradvājagottaṁ brāhmaṇaṁ etadavocuṁ:
segs.e: Then several students, pupils of one of the Bhāradvāja brahmins, approached a forest grove while collecting firewood. They saw the Buddha sitting down cross-legged at the root of a certain sal tree, his body set straight, and mindfulness brought to the present. Seeing this, they went up to Bhāradvāja and said to him,
“Please sir, you should know this.

segs.p: Asukasmiṁ vanasaṇḍe samaṇo nisinno pallaṅkaṁ ābhujitvā ujuṁ kāyaṁ paṇidhāya parimukhaṁ satiṁ upaṭṭhapetvā”.
segs.e: In such-and-such forest grove the ascetic Gotama is sitting down cross-legged, his body set straight, and mindfulness brought to the present.”

segs.p: Atha kho bhāradvājagotto brāhmaṇo tehi māṇavakehi saddhiṁ yena so vanasaṇḍo tenupasaṅkami.
segs.e: Then Bhāradvāja together with those young students went to that forest grove

segs.p: Addasā kho bhagavantaṁ tasmiṁ vanasaṇḍe nisinnaṁ pallaṅkaṁ ābhujitvā ujuṁ kāyaṁ paṇidhāya parimukhaṁ satiṁ upaṭṭhapetvā.
segs.e: where he saw the Buddha sitting down cross-legged, his body set straight, and mindfulness brought to the present.

segs.p: Disvāna yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi:
segs.e: He went up to the Buddha and addressed him in verse:
“Deep in the jungle so full of terrors,
you’ve plunged into the empty, desolate wilderness.
Still, steady, and graceful:
how beautifully you meditate, mendicant!

segs.p: Na yattha gītaṁ napi yattha vāditaṁ,
segs.e: Where there is no song or music,
a lonely sage resorts to the wilderness.
This strikes me as an amazing thing,
that you dwell so joyfully alone in the jungle.
I suppose you wish to be reborn in the company
of the supreme world-sovereign <j>of the Third Heaven.
Is that why you resort to the desolate wilderness,
to practice fervor for attaining divinity?”
“Any wishes and hopes that are always attached
to the many and various realms—
the prayers sprung from the root of unknowing—
I’ve eliminated them all down to the root.
So I’m wishless, unattached, uninvolved;
amongst all things, my vision is clear.
I’ve attained the state of grace, <j>the supreme awakening;
I meditate alone, brahmin, and self-assured.”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, bhāradvājagotto brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When he had spoken, Bhāradvāja said to the Buddha,
“Excellent, worthy Gotama! Excellent! …
From this day forth, may the worthy Gotama remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.”
Linked Discourses 7.19
2. Lay Followers
The Brahmin Who Provided for His Mother
At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: Atha kho mātuposako brāhmaṇo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṁ sammodi.
segs.e: Then a brahmin who provided for his mother went up to the Buddha, and exchanged greetings with him.

segs.p: Sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho mātuposako brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side and said to the Buddha,

segs.p: “ahañhi, bho gotama, dhammena bhikkhaṁ pariyesāmi, dhammena bhikkhaṁ pariyesitvā mātāpitaro posemi.
segs.e: “Worthy Gotama, I seek alms by legitimate means, which I use to provide for my mother and father.

segs.p: Kaccāhaṁ, bho gotama, evaṅkārī kiccakārī homī”ti?
segs.e: In doing so, am I doing my duty?”
“Indeed, brahmin, in so doing you are doing your duty.

segs.p: Yo kho, brāhmaṇa, dhammena bhikkhaṁ pariyesati, dhammena bhikkhaṁ pariyesitvā mātāpitaro poseti, bahuṁ so puññaṁ pasavatīti.
segs.e: Whoever seeks alms by legitimate means, and uses them to provide for their mother and father brims with much merit.
A mortal provides for their mother
and father by legitimate means;
because they serve
their parents like this,
they’re praised in this life by the astute,
and they depart to rejoice in heaven.”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, mātuposako brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When he said this, the brahmin who provided for his mother said to the Buddha,
“Excellent, worthy Gotama! Excellent! …

segs.p: upāsakaṁ maṁ bhavaṁ gotamo dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṁ saraṇaṁ gatan”ti.
segs.e: From this day forth, may the worthy Gotama remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.”
Linked Discourses 7.20
2. Lay Followers
An Almsman
At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: Atha kho bhikkhako brāhmaṇo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṁ sammodi.
segs.e: Then a brahmin almsman went up to the Buddha, and exchanged greetings with him.

segs.p: Sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho bhikkhako brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side and said to the Buddha,

segs.p: “ahampi kho, bho gotama, bhikkhako, bhavampi bhikkhako, idha no kiṁ nānākaraṇan”ti?
segs.e: “Worthy Gotama, both you and I are almsmen. What, then, is the difference between us?”
“You don’t become an almsman
just by begging alms from others.
One who has undertaken domestic duties
has not yet become a mendicant.
But one living a spiritual life
who has banished both merit and evil,
and wanders having appraised the world,
is said to be a mendicant.”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, bhikkhako brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When he had spoken, the brahmin almsman said to the Buddha,
“Excellent, worthy Gotama! Excellent! …

segs.p: upāsakaṁ maṁ bhavaṁ gotamo dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṁ saraṇaṁ gatan”ti.
segs.e: From this day forth, may the worthy Gotama remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.”
Linked Discourses 7.21
2. Lay Followers
With Saṅgārava
At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena saṅgāravo nāma brāhmaṇo sāvatthiyaṁ paṭivasati udakasuddhiko, udakena parisuddhiṁ pacceti, sāyaṁ pātaṁ udakorohanānuyogamanuyutto viharati.
segs.e: Now at that time there was a brahmin named Saṅgārava staying in Sāvatthī. He practiced purification by water, believing in purification by water. He lived committed to the practice of immersing himself in water at daybreak and dusk.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā ānando pubbaṇhasamayaṁ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya sāvatthiṁ piṇḍāya pāvisi.
segs.e: Then Venerable Ānanda robed up in the morning and, taking his bowl and robe, entered Sāvatthī for alms.

segs.p: Sāvatthiyaṁ piṇḍāya caritvā pacchābhattaṁ piṇḍapātapaṭikkanto yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: He wandered for alms in Sāvatthī. After the meal, on his return from almsround, he went to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him,

segs.p: “idha, bhante, saṅgāravo nāma brāhmaṇo sāvatthiyaṁ paṭivasati udakasuddhiko, udakena suddhiṁ pacceti, sāyaṁ pātaṁ udakorohanānuyogamanuyutto viharati.
segs.e: “Sir, there is a brahmin named Saṅgārava staying in Sāvatthī. He practices purification by water, believing in purification by water. He lives devoted to ritual bathing at daybreak and dusk.

segs.p: Sādhu, bhante, bhagavā yena saṅgāravassa brāhmaṇassa nivesanaṁ tenupasaṅkamatu anukampaṁ upādāyā”ti.
segs.e: Please visit him at his home out of sympathy.”
The Buddha consented with silence.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā pubbaṇhasamayaṁ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya yena saṅgāravassa brāhmaṇassa nivesanaṁ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi.
segs.e: Then the Buddha robed up in the morning and, taking his bowl and robe, went to the home of the brahmin Saṅgārava, and sat down on the seat spread out.

segs.p: Atha kho saṅgāravo brāhmaṇo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṁ sammodi.
segs.e: Then the brahmin Saṅgārava went up to the Buddha, and exchanged greetings with him.

segs.p: Sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho saṅgāravaṁ brāhmaṇaṁ bhagavā etadavoca:
segs.e: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side. The Buddha said to him,

segs.p: “saccaṁ kira tvaṁ, brāhmaṇa, udakasuddhiko, udakena suddhiṁ paccesi, sāyaṁ pātaṁ udakorohanānuyogamanuyutto viharasī”ti?
segs.e: “Is it really true, brahmin, that you practice purification by water, believing in purification by water; that you live committed to the practice of immersing yourself in water at daybreak and dusk?”
“Yes, worthy Gotama.”

segs.p: “Kiṁ pana tvaṁ, brāhmaṇa, atthavasaṁ sampassamāno udakasuddhiko, udakasuddhiṁ paccesi, sāyaṁ pātaṁ udakorohanānuyogamanuyutto viharasī”ti?
segs.e: “But brahmin, for what reason do you practice purification by water?”

segs.p: “Idha me, bho gotama, yaṁ divā pāpakammaṁ kataṁ hoti, taṁ sāyaṁ nhānena pavāhemi, yaṁ rattiṁ pāpakammaṁ kataṁ hoti taṁ pātaṁ nhānena pavāhemi.
segs.e: “It’s because, Worthy Gotama, whatever bad deeds I’ve done during the day I rinse off by bathing at dusk; and whatever bad deeds I’ve done during the night, I rinse off by bathing at dawn.

segs.p: Imaṁ khvāhaṁ, bho gotama, atthavasaṁ sampassamāno udakasuddhiko, udakena suddhiṁ paccemi, sāyaṁ pātaṁ udakorohanānuyogamanuyutto viharāmī”ti.
segs.e: That’s the reason why I practice purification by water.”
“The teaching is a lake, brahmin, <j>into which ethics are the stairs,
unclouded, praised by the fine to the good.
There the knowledge masters go to bathe,
and cross to the far shore with dry limbs.”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, saṅgāravo brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When he had spoken, Saṅgārava said to the Buddha,
“Excellent, worthy Gotama! Excellent! …

segs.p: upāsakaṁ maṁ bhavaṁ gotamo dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṁ saraṇaṁ gatan”ti.
segs.e: From this day forth, may the worthy Gotama remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.”
Linked Discourses 7.22
2. Lay Followers
At Khomadussa
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sakkesu viharati khomadussaṁ nāmaṁ sakyānaṁ nigamo.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying in the land of the Sakyans, where they have a town named Khomadussa.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā pubbaṇhasamayaṁ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya khomadussaṁ nigamaṁ piṇḍāya pāvisi.
segs.e: Then the Buddha robed up in the morning and, taking his bowl and robe, entered Khomadussa for alms.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena khomadussakā brāhmaṇagahapatikā sabhāyaṁ sannipatitā honti kenacideva karaṇīyena, devo ca ekamekaṁ phusāyati.
segs.e: Now at that time the brahmins and householders of Khomadussa were gathered in the council hall for some business, while a gentle rain drizzled down.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā yena sā sabhā tenupasaṅkami.
segs.e: Then the Buddha approached that council.

segs.p: Addasaṁsu khomadussakā brāhmaṇagahapatikā bhagavantaṁ dūratova āgacchantaṁ.
segs.e: The brahmins and householders saw the Buddha coming off in the distance,
and said,

segs.p: “ke ca muṇḍakā samaṇakā, ke ca sabhādhammaṁ jānissantī”ti?
segs.e: “Who are these shavelings, these fake ascetics? Don’t they understand the council rules?”

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā khomadussake brāhmaṇagahapatike gāthāya ajjhabhāsi:
segs.e: Then the Buddha addressed the brahmins and householders of Khomadussa in verse:
“If good people are not present it is no true council;

segs.p: Santo na te ye na vadanti dhammaṁ;
segs.e: and those whose speak against principle <j>are not good people.
Having given up greed, hate, and delusion,
speakers of principle are good people.”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, khomadussakā brāhmaṇagahapatikā bhagavantaṁ etadavocuṁ:
segs.e: When he had spoken, the brahmins and householders of Khomadussa said to the Buddha,
“Excellent, worthy Gotama! Excellent!

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bho gotama, nikkujjitaṁ vā ukkujjeyya, paṭicchannaṁ vā vivareyya, mūḷhassa vā maggaṁ ācikkheyya, andhakāre vā telapajjotaṁ dhāreyya: ‘cakkhumanto rūpāni dakkhantī’ti; evamevaṁ bhotā gotamena anekapariyāyena dhammo pakāsito.
segs.e: As if he were righting the overturned, or revealing the hidden, or pointing out the path to the lost, or lighting a lamp in the dark so people with clear eyes can see what’s there, worthy Gotama has made the teaching clear in many ways.

segs.p: Ete mayaṁ bhavantaṁ gotamaṁ saraṇaṁ gacchāma dhammañca bhikkhusaṅghañca.
segs.e: We go for refuge to the worthy Gotama, to the teaching, and to the mendicant Saṅgha.

segs.p: Upāsake no bhavaṁ gotamo dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupete saraṇaṁ gate”ti.
segs.e: From this day forth, may the worthy Gotama remember us as lay followers who have gone for refuge for life.”
